page: Microsoft Azure D16ps_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DPSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The architecture is arm64, providing a single thread per core with no hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it contains no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 28878.29 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9616.0. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1119.0 and a weak Passmark CPU encryption score of 2602.32. Memory bandwidth is measured at 1127.64 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 133.94 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. The server demonstrates average capabilities in database operations, scoring 11221.3 on Passmark, and achieves 20.86 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks.

The ARM-based architecture offers a resource-dense configuration with dedicated physical cores, which can translate to consistent execution times and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads. However, the lack of x86 instruction sets and weak single-core performance present clear tradeoffs for legacy applications or single-threaded tasks. This server is suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose workloads that benefit from dedicated ARM cores.
